name: ANDORRA

flag.title: Flag of Andorra
flag.note: Blue, yellow & red with royal coat of arms

lead: Andorra is a tiny country in the Pyrenees mountains, between France and Spain. You can drive across it in 30 minutes. Two princes rule it at once: the French president and a Spanish bishop. This has lasted over 700 years.

facts.label: Money
facts.sub: Not EU, but uses the euro currency

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Andorra sits inside the Pyrenees mountains. Its average height is nearly 2,000 m. Rivers carved every valley, and pine and fir forests cover the slopes.
Two main rivers rush down rocky gorges into Spain. Mountains ring Andorra, so it has no coast, port, or airport. Visitors drive in over mountain passes.
animals: The bearded vulture (lammergeier) is Andorra's national bird. Its wings are wider than a family sofa. It lives mostly on bones. It drops them onto rocks to crack them open.
The isard is a goat-antelope that bounds over snowy ridges up to 3,000 m. A dark mask makes it look like a cartoon bandit.
culture: People in Andorra speak Catalan. Romanesque stone churches in Andorra la Vella are nearly 900 years old. Sant Esteve still rings its bells each morning.
Every September, parishes celebrate with folk dances and giant paper-mâché figures called gegants. Caldea, a spa shaped like a glass rocket, is Europe's largest spa complex.
history: In 1278 the Bishop of Urgell and the Count of Foix quarrelled over Andorra. They agreed to share it equally. This deal, a paréage, made a co-principality that has never ended.
In 1607 Henry IV became King of France. The co-prince title then passed to every French president. Andorra's first written constitution came in 1993.
wows: Two co-princes lead Andorra: the French president and a Spanish bishop.
Andorra is the only country where Catalan is the sole official language.
At 1,023 m above sea level, Andorra la Vella is Europe's highest capital.
Andorra has no army and has been at peace for over 700 years.
Grandvalira is the largest ski area in the whole Pyrenees.
Sales tax is just 4.5%, so goods cost 20–40% less than next door.
Over 8 million tourists visit yearly, nearly 100 for every resident.

myths.myth: The Pyrenees are Europe's tallest mountains
myths.fact: The Alps are taller. Mont Blanc is 4,807 m. The top Pyrenean peak, Aneto, is 3,404 m.

myths.myth: You can take a train to Andorra
myths.fact: Andorra has no railway. The nearest stations are in France and Spain.
